sample-307-1: My electricity bill has gone up three winters in a row. Before we invite the largest electricity consumers in the country into Maine, somebody ought to do the math on what it means for the rest of us. A pause to study it isn't radical — it's what any careful household would do.
sample-307-2: I work in software and I'm not against data centers. I'm against building them before we know who pays for the transmission upgrades. Other states got this wrong and their ratepayers are covering the difference. Maine has one chance to get it right the first time.
sample-307-3: Our region has been waiting decades for the kind of investment a data center could bring to the old mill sites. Jobs, tax base, a reason for young people to stay. A statewide moratorium treats Millinocket the same as Portland, and we are not the same. Let towns decide for themselves.
sample-307-4: A blanket moratorium sends exactly the wrong signal to employers considering Maine. We support the Coordination Council concept, but pairing study with prohibition tells the market that Maine is closed. Study first, restrict only if the evidence supports it.
sample-307-5: I don't know yet whether these projects are good for the St. John Valley. What I do know is nobody has explained the water usage numbers in plain language. Whatever the committee decides, please require the companies to publish their consumption where we can all read it.
